title: Bill Crego's band and pianist Joe Garrow
summary: Hazel names members of the band at the old Absinthe House and describes Garrow's arranging and limited soloing.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: And who did Bill Crego play with?

He played with, with Naylor. Well, but here, he had the band, that's the, he, he's the first band I worked with in the quality. He had the band at the old Abson house. Uh, see, not, not where the bar is, of the old Abson, but in the, in the, in the back where Piron plays. I'm not, I mean where Pichon, where Fats plays. Well, that was the club, you see. And it was owned by two different people. The bar, well, that's the original bar across from the famous door. That's the bar that was at, at Arberville Street. And, and, and that guy owned the, but Tony DeFranco was the fellow that owned the, the club in the back. And all that was, all that was doing probation, you see. And, uh, we had, uh, Bill Crego, a fellow by the name of Joe Lambious, was a banjo player. And, uh, Red, Red Long, no, no, a fellow by the name of Joe Garrow, was a piano player. He played, he played wonderful, wonderful, uh, time, and good, real good beat, but don't ask him to take chorus, cause he couldn't take chorus to save his life. He's, uh, like a guy that I, I worked for in New York, an arranger. That, make a sit down and write, he'd, he'd, he'd make a whole arrangement, Bill, on the, on the way home on the subway, you know. Sit down there without piano, without an instrument, anything else, and make out a whole arrangement. And I see him make arrangements that Pollock's band couldn't cut. Benny, you know, take him, let the bands play him and sell him to the different band. And he brought a couple of things around there to band, I'm talking about when Benny Goodman and all those guys were with Pollock. And the band just couldn't cut his arrangement. And the guy couldn't take the chorus, don't ask him to take the chorus. He, but, sit, didn't play those chords, you know. He had a real good fine beat, but just couldn't, couldn't play by himself, that's all.
